_note: Real, verified external events in Brazil during the Olist data window (2016-2018). Each event and brief cites its public sources. Compiled for WhyChain on 2026-10-22; briefs are paraphrased summaries, not copies of the articles.

events.name: Carnival holiday 2017
events.affects: Working days for federal agencies, commerce and logistics nationwide
events.summary: Carnival Monday and Tuesday (27-28 Feb 2017) were optional federal holidays, and Ash Wednesday (1 Mar) was optional until 14:00 (Portaria MP 369/2016). State and municipal rules varied.

events.name: Correios workers' national strike (Apr-May 2017)
events.summary: Correios workers began an open-ended national strike on the night of 26 Apr 2017 over privatization fears, layoffs and branch closures; the TST ordered 80% of staff to keep working. By 9 May workers had returned almost everywhere and Correios expected the delayed parcels to be cleared that week.

events.name: National general strike against labour and pension reforms
events.affects: Urban transport, some airport staff and postal workers in major capitals
events.summary: Nine union federations called a one-day general strike on 28 Apr 2017 against the labour and pension reforms. Bus and metro stoppages were expected in capitals including Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Brasilia and Salvador; it overlapped with the ongoing Correios strike.

events.name: Correios discontinues e-Sedex
events.affects: Correios shipping options and freight costs for online sellers
events.summary: Correios withdrew e-Sedex, a discounted express service for small and mid-sized online stores, on 19 Jun 2017, leaving Sedex and PAC as the options for e-commerce. An earlier attempt to end it on 1 Jan 2017 had been blocked by a court injunction.

events.name: Correios restricted-delivery (risk) areas in Rio de Janeiro
events.affects: Correios home delivery of parcels in designated risk areas of Rio de Janeiro
events.summary: Correios does not deliver parcels to homes in areas its security department classifies as high-risk; those parcels go to the nearest Correios unit for pickup. Long-running practice (at least four years as of Feb 2018); start_date is the earliest report used, not the policy start.

events.name: Correios workers' national strike (Sep-Oct 2017)
events.summary: Correios workers struck from the night of 19 Sep 2017 over the 2017/18 wage deal and benefit cuts; the TST ordered 80% minimum staffing. Unions accepted a TST-brokered deal on 6 Oct, staff returned on 9 Oct, and Correios expected normal service within five business days.

events.name: Black Friday 2017 (eve through Cyber Monday)
events.affects: E-commerce order volumes and parcel networks
events.summary: Black Friday fell on 24 Nov 2017. Ebit reported R$2.1bn of online sales that day (+10.3% y/y, orders +14%) and R$3.2bn on 6.1m orders (+16.1%) over 23-27 Nov.

events.name: Record cargo theft in Rio de Janeiro state (2017)
events.affects: Road freight and parcel deliveries in Rio de Janeiro state, including Correios operations
events.summary: Rio de Janeiro state recorded a record 10,599 cargo robberies in 2017 (ISP data), up 7.3% on 2016. Correios reported 2,339 robbery incidents against its operations in Rio in Jan-Sep 2017, against 1,239 in Jan-Sep 2018.

events.name: Carnival holiday 2018
events.affects: Working days for federal agencies, commerce and logistics nationwide
events.summary: Carnival Monday and Tuesday (12-13 Feb 2018) were optional federal holidays, and Ash Wednesday (14 Feb) was optional until 14:00 (Portaria MP 468 of 22 Dec 2017). State and municipal rules varied.

events.name: Severe storm in Rio de Janeiro city
events.affects: Urban traffic and infrastructure in Rio de Janeiro city (no postal-specific impact reported)
events.summary: Heavy rain on 15 Feb 2018 led Rio's city government to declare its highest crisis stage. At least four people died, neighbourhoods flooded, avenues closed and power was cut in parts of the city.

events.name: Federal intervention in Rio de Janeiro public security
events.affects: Public security operations in Rio de Janeiro state
events.summary: Decree 9,288 of 16 Feb 2018 placed public security in Rio de Janeiro state under federal intervention until 31 Dec 2018, with Army General Walter Braga Netto in command of the state police and fire brigade.

events.name: Correios R$3 emergency surcharge on parcels to Rio metro area
events.affects: Correios parcel prices for deliveries to Rio de Janeiro city and metropolitan region
events.summary: On 27 Feb 2018 Correios announced a R$3 surcharge per parcel to Rio city and its metro area, citing extreme violence against its staff and vehicles, due from 6 Mar. A Procon-RJ injunction suspended it in March, an appeals court reinstated it in April, and Correios ended it on 16 Nov 2018.

events.name: Correios PAC/Sedex price increase
events.affects: Correios parcel freight prices for e-commerce sellers
events.summary: A Correios PAC and Sedex price adjustment was due on 6 Mar 2018: about 8% between capitals per Correios, up to 51% on some routes per Mercado Livre. Courts granted injunctions to Mercado Livre (6 Mar) and to the e-commerce association ABComm (April).

events.name: Correios workers' national strike over health plan (Mar 2018)
events.summary: Correios workers began an open-ended national strike on 12 Mar 2018 against health-plan changes. After a TST ruling the same day, the federation called it off on 13 Mar with return to work on 14 Mar; Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo unions still had assemblies pending.

events.name: Truckers' strike (greve dos caminhoneiros)
events.affects: Road freight, fuel supply and parcel deliveries nationwide
events.summary: Truck drivers blocked highways across Brazil from 21 May 2018 over diesel prices, causing nationwide fuel, food and medicine shortages. The government conceded diesel cuts and a minimum freight table, and most protests had ended by 1 Jun.

events.name: Correios service suspensions during truckers' strike
events.summary: On 23 May 2018 Correios suspended Sedex 10, Sedex 12 and Sedex Hoje and extended Sedex, PAC and letter deadlines while the strike lasted. On 28 May it said it could not guarantee delivery deadlines for any service. The date full service resumed is not confirmed.

briefs.title: Correios strike, April-May 2017
briefs.body: Postal workers represented by the Fentect federation began an open-ended national strike at 22:00 on 26 April 2017. The federation cited fears of privatization and layoffs, the planned closure of more than 200 branches, and the company's finances; demands also included hiring, branch security and a return to daily delivery. The Superior Labour Court (TST) ordered unions to keep 80% of staff working. On 2 May, Sao Paulo workers voted to stay out. By 9 May workers had returned in almost all of the country (99.85% at work, per Correios), and the company said it expected delayed parcels to be cleared that week.

briefs.title: Correios ends e-Sedex
briefs.body: In late 2016 Correios announced it would discontinue e-Sedex, a discounted express service for small and mid-sized online retailers, from 1 January 2017. A federal court injunction in December 2016 initially blocked the move. Correios finally withdrew the service on 19 June 2017 under a new commercial policy, leaving online sellers with Sedex, PAC and reverse-logistics packages. The e-commerce association ABComm had estimated freight costs would rise about 30%, with the heaviest effect on smaller sellers and on customers in the interior, who have fewer carrier alternatives.

briefs.title: Delivery restrictions in Rio de Janeiro risk areas
briefs.body: Correios does not deliver parcels to homes in areas its security department classifies as high-risk, using public-security risk maps and the record of robberies of its cargo vehicles. Affected parcels are routed to the nearest Correios unit for customer pickup. In February 2018 Agencia Brasil reported the practice had been in place for at least four years. An August 2017 report found some online retailers refusing to ship to certain Rio postal codes or redirecting orders to Correios branches, and said Rio was the only Southeast state where online retail revenue fell in the first half of 2017.

briefs.title: Correios strike, September-October 2017
briefs.body: Correios workers began a national strike on the night of 19 September 2017, the second postal strike of the year; at first 28 of the 31 Fentect-affiliated unions joined. Unions sought an 8% raise and opposed proposed cuts to benefits. Correios said 93% of staff were working on the first day, and the TST ordered 80% minimum staffing. On 6 October unions accepted a TST-brokered agreement with a 2.07% raise. Staff returned on 9 October, and Correios estimated services would be back to normal within five business days.

briefs.title: Black Friday 2017
briefs.body: Black Friday fell on Friday 24 November 2017. According to Ebit, Brazilian e-commerce billed R$2.1bn that day, up 10.3% year on year, with orders up 14%. Over the extended period from the eve of Black Friday (23 November) to Cyber Monday (27 November), revenue reached R$3.2bn (+8.7%) on 6.1 million orders (+16.1%). The average ticket fell 6.4% to R$520 as retailers offered deeper discounts. The sources reviewed contained no consolidated report of Black Friday 2017 delivery delays.

briefs.title: Cargo theft in Rio de Janeiro, 2017
briefs.body: Data from Rio's Public Security Institute (ISP) showed a record 10,599 cargo robberies in the state in 2017, 7.3% more than the 9,874 in 2016, or about 29 per day. The capital accounted for 5,371 cases, the Baixada Fluminense 3,167, Niteroi and Sao Goncalo 1,586, and the interior 475. The state attributed a decline from September 2017 to a joint state-federal task force. Correios later reported 2,339 robbery incidents against its operations in Rio in January-September 2017, falling to 1,239 in the same period of 2018.

briefs.title: Holiday calendar: Carnival 2018
briefs.body: The federal government set Monday 12 and Tuesday 13 February 2018 as optional holidays for Carnival, and Ash Wednesday, 14 February, as optional until 14:00 (Ministry of Planning Portaria 468 of 22 December 2017). Because Carnival is not a statutory national holiday, closures followed state and municipal decrees and employer decisions, and schedules varied by city. In practice much of Brazil worked a shortened week in mid-February 2018.

briefs.title: Rio de Janeiro storm, 15 February 2018
briefs.body: Heavy rain hit the city of Rio de Janeiro in the early hours of 15 February 2018, and the city government declared its highest risk level (crisis stage). At least four people died. Several neighbourhoods flooded, avenues were closed, a hospital was flooded, and power was cut in parts of Rio and the Baixada Fluminense. The sources reviewed reported no postal-specific disruption.

briefs.title: Federal intervention in Rio de Janeiro
briefs.body: On 16 February 2018 President Michel Temer signed Decree 9,288, placing public security in Rio de Janeiro state under federal intervention until 31 December 2018. The measure was limited to public security. Army General Walter Souza Braga Netto took command of the state's civil and military police and fire brigade. Both houses of Congress approved the decree within days, and the intervention ran until its scheduled end on 31 December 2018.

briefs.title: Correios surcharge on Rio-bound parcels
briefs.body: On 27 February 2018 Correios announced a R$3 emergency surcharge per parcel delivered to Rio de Janeiro city and its metropolitan region, citing extreme levels of violence and the cost of protecting staff, parcels and units. Letters and parcels to the state interior were exempt, and the fee was due to start on 6 March. A federal court injunction sought by Procon-RJ suspended it in March; in April the president of the TRF2 appeals court reinstated it. Correios ended the fee on 16 November 2018, citing an average 60% fall in robberies in January-September 2018 compared with 2017.

briefs.title: Correios parcel price increase, March 2018
briefs.body: A Correios PAC and Sedex price adjustment was due to take effect on 6 March 2018. Correios described an increase of about 8% for shipments between state capitals; Mercado Livre said some interior and interstate routes rose by up to 51%, with an average of 29%. On 6 March a Sao Paulo federal court granted Mercado Livre an injunction suspending the increase for its users. In April the e-commerce association ABComm obtained an injunction capping Sedex and PAC increases at 8% for its members.

briefs.title: Correios strike, March 2018
briefs.body: Correios workers began an open-ended national strike on Monday 12 March 2018 (from 22:00 on 11 March for night shifts). They opposed health-plan changes that introduced monthly fees and removed dependants, as well as outsourcing and privatization. On 12 March the TST ruled that employees would pay 30% of plan costs and Correios 70%. Fentect called off the national strike on 13 March, with return to work on 14 March; Correios said 24 of the 32 striking unions had voted to return by that evening, while Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo still had assemblies scheduled.

briefs.title: Truckers' strike, May 2018
briefs.body: Truck drivers began blocking highways across Brazil on 21 May 2018 in protest at rising diesel prices. Within days more than 20 states were affected and shortages of fuel, food and medicine spread; by 29 May fuel shortages affected 15 state capitals. A 23 May deal including a 10% Petrobras diesel cut failed to end the protests. The government then conceded further diesel cuts and a minimum freight-rate table, published on 31 May. Most protests had ended by 1 June. On 23 May Correios suspended Sedex 10, Sedex 12 and Sedex Hoje and extended Sedex, PAC and letter deadlines; on 28 May it said it could not guarantee delivery deadlines for any domestic or international service.
